items.title: Manchester Airports Group Data on 8.8 Million People Leaked After Ransom Refusal
items.one_liner: Manchester Airports Group leaks 8.8 million user records online after refusing extortion demands.
items.summary: Manchester Airports Group (MAG) suffered a data breach after the FulcrumSec extortion gang exfiltrated car park, lounge, and Fast Track booking records containing personal information for 8.8 million individuals. The attackers stated they accessed third-party hosted databases after finding administrative API keys exposed in plaintext within frontend JavaScript files across airport root domains. MAG refused a ransom demand, prompting the extortion group to leak roughly 550 gigabytes of uncompressed data, including email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registrations, and residential IP addresses.
items.bottom_line: Exposed administrative API keys in frontend JavaScript can lead to catastrophic enterprise database breaches and data leaks.

items.title: CSS:the bomb inside your inbox
items.one_liner: Webmail CSS sanitizer bypasses and overlooked HTML label elements enable attackers to hijack user interfaces and manipulate Microsoft Outlook.
items.summary: PortSwigger researcher Gareth Heyes has published a security analysis detailing how discrepancies between webmail CSS sanitizers and browser rendering engines can be weaponized to hijack user interfaces, exfiltrate tokens, and steal credentials. The research highlights that HTML label elements are frequently overlooked by sanitizers and can inherit form click actions to manipulate application interfaces. Specifically, a vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook allows an attacker using a crafted email message to control the Outlook UI ribbon and pin messages without user interaction. The paper also examines how CSS pseudo-elements like :before and :after can inject hidden content to execute indirect prompt attacks against AI-driven browsers such as OpenAI Atlas.
key_facts: Affected products: Outlook, Yahoo Mail, AOL Mail, Fastmail, ProtonMail, Gmail, OpenAI Atlas
items.bottom_line: Discrepancies between HTML sanitizers and browser parsing engines allow attackers to execute privilege escalation and UI redressing via standard email messages.

items.title: Meta Ads Push StreamRat Android Trojan That Can Gain Near-Complete Device Control
items.one_liner: A sophisticated Android trojan is using Meta ads and VPN-based evasion to gain full device control.
items.summary: A sophisticated Android banking trojan called StreamRat is targeting Spanish-speaking users through fraudulent streaming advertisements on Meta platforms. The malware gains near-complete device control by tricking users into granting Accessibility permissions and setting it as the default Home application. It employs a unique VPN-based dropper that disrupts the internet connectivity of other apps to potentially evade security reputation checks during the infection process. Once active, StreamRat can capture keystrokes, display credential-stealing overlays, and use the MediaProjection API for remote screen monitoring.
key_facts: Permissions: Accessibility, VPN, Default Home app
items.bottom_line: Users must avoid sideloading streaming apps that request unrelated system permissions like Accessibility or VPN control.

claims.text: The campaign reached over 570,000 Meta accounts.
claims.support_span: ThreatFabric said the campaign's advertisement focused on Spain and reached an estimated 570,950 Meta accounts in the European Union that saw it at least once, with totals for infected devices and confirmed victims remaining unreported.

claims.text: The malware uses the MediaProjection API for screen capture.
claims.support_span: For a visible screen capture, StreamRat invokes Android's MediaProjection application programming interface (API), which displays a consent dialog and is typically identified by a screen-sharing indicator.

claims.text: The dropper uses a VPN connection to route device traffic.
claims.support_span: Before fetching the final payload, the dropper requests permission to establish a VPN connection. Once approved, the VPN routes device traffic into a nonfunctional interface while excluding the dropper itself.

items.title: CVE-2026-84304 (HIGH 8.7): gRPC-Go is the Go language implementation of gRPC. Prior to 1.83.1, internal/transport/transport.go stores ea…
items.summary: gRPC-Go is the Go language implementation of gRPC. Prior to 1.83.1, internal/transport/transport.go stores each fragmented HTTP/2 DATA frame as a separate recvMsg in recvBuffer, so millions of one-byte frames can consume disproportionate heap memory even when payload bytes remain within connection and stream flow-control windows. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use concurrent multiplexed streams to exhaust process memory and cause a runtime panic or out-of-memory termination. Receive-buffer compaction is enabled by default and can be controlled temporarily with GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_RECEIVE_BUFFER_COMPACTION.

items.summary: Hugging Face introduces BenchMIRT, a multidimensional Item Response Theory method for auditing LLM benchmarks at the individual prompt level. items.one_liner: IBM and Confluent deploy real-time time series foundation models directly into Flink streaming pipelines on AWS.
items.summary: IBM has integrated its Granite-based Time Series Foundation Models (TSFM) directly into Confluent Cloud to offer stream-native analytics and forecasting. The service is initially available via Confluent Cloud on AWS, with planned rollout to hybrid and on-premises Confluent Platform deployments.

items.one_liner: A new tool for reverse engineering stripped binaries that uses behavioral fingerprints instead of static signatures to bypass compiler optimization differences.
items.summary: fnprint is a training-free, cross-compiler tool for identifying functions in stripped binaries by analyzing their behavior through microexecution. It operates by running each function in a tiny emulator with synthetic inputs to record side effects and hash them into a behavioral fingerprint. This approach overcomes the limitations of byte signatures and CFG matchers, which often fail when code is recompiled or optimization levels change. The tool is a practical implementation of the 'Blanket Execution' concept from USENIX Security 2014.

items.summary: We introduce NeoMME, a family of 260M and 800M multilingual multimodal encoders. items.title: Web App Pentesting in the AI Era
items.one_liner: A web application pentester evaluates AI-assisted vulnerability analysis, breaking down the roles of models, inference engines, and harnesses.
items.summary: A web application pentester shares insights from three hands-on months evaluating AI-assisted vulnerability analysis using both frontier and local models. The analysis clarifies the three distinct components of LLM-based AI systems: the underlying model acting as the parameter-based brain, the read-only inference engine that processes inputs, and the harness responsible for memory, tool execution, and state orchestration. While early media coverage was dominated by hyperbole, recent advancements show that both large and small models can provide meaningful utility to security practitioners. The research highlights that separating these architectural layers is essential for calibrating expectations around automated web application testing.
items.bottom_line: Security professionals can effectively leverage AI models for vulnerability analysis by understanding the distinct operational roles of models, inference engines, and harnesses.
